lines.text: In the kingdom of Aldmere, you are measured once, at sixteen, and it decides the rest of your life. I was measured once. I lit nothing at all.
So they sent me to Greyhollow, at the edge of the world. A year later, it had a harbour, a bathhouse, a Compact with the north, and a dog the size of a horse.
And now the King wanted to measure me again, in front of his whole court. If I refused, every lord who had signed for me would hang.
On the third morning south, I woke before dawn, and I couldn't find Greyhollow.
The threads were all still there. Every one. But they had gone faint, like voices in another room.
Distance. I did warn you. Away from you and your land, they stop growing. They don't slip. They simply wait.
Like dough in a cold kitchen.
You remember the things I say. I find that very unsettling.
The three threads riding with me were the opposite. Wren's, Oswin's and Ash's. Close and warm, and still growing. As if I'd packed three hearths, and left the rest of the house in the cold.
If you've finished staring at the sky, my lord, Oswin has burned the porridge.
I did not burn it. I toasted it. It's a northern custom.
At noon, one of our stable boys caught us at a ford, on a pony with no sense of direction, waving a letter in Bram's square, careful hand.
My lord. Nobody has grown since you left. Nobody has slipped. Magister Thorne will say something clever about bread.
Rook, Birk and Tarn have eaten a boot. It was my boot. I was wearing it.
Wren laughed so hard she fell off her log. Oswin had to sit down. Even Ilse smiled, and then pretended she hadn't.
Your father's rider came the day after you left. I am sorry, my lord. I read it. It is enclosed.
Lucan. Whatever they summon you for, do not come.
Two lines. In seventeen years, my father had never once told me not to come. He had only ever told me to go.
First he tells you never to touch a Stone again. Now this. Lucan, has it ever occurred to you that your father knows something?
My father knows the price of grain, and the names of Maric's horses. He has never known anything about me.
I put it inside my coat, beside my wards' letter. Six words, four of them spelled wrong. Then I turned my horse south again.
Two days later, the forest ended, and the midlands began. Rich, flat, golden land. And the closer we came to the river, the greyer it got.
That evening, we rode into a village where nobody looked up.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter sixty-two, coming soon.
